title: Nut-Free Chocolate Birthday Cupcakes
shortDescription: Rich chocolate cupcakes with a fudgy crumb, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake, made with zero nut ingredients.
description: These cupcakes are deep, chocolatey, and completely safe for school lunches or nut-free birthday parties. I tested this batch in my home kitchen three times to get the crumb soft but sturdy enough for piping.
ingredients: Rainbow sprinkles, nut-free brand, for topping
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, cocoa powder, sugar, baking soda, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, mix buttermilk, oil, egg, and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the wet mix into the dry mix. Stir just until combined.
Add hot water and stir gently. The batter will be thin, that is normal.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs.
Cool cupcakes in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully.
Beat softened butter until fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add powdered sugar, cocoa powder, and milk. Beat until smooth and pipeable.
Pipe frosting high onto cooled cupcakes and finish with nut-free sprinkles.
tips: Check every sprinkle and food coloring label. Some are processed in facilities that handle nuts.
Use hot water, not boiling. It blooms the cocoa and makes the crumb extra soft.
Let cupcakes cool completely before frosting or the buttercream will slide off.
Bake one test cupcake first if your oven runs hot, so the rest do not overbake.

faq.question: Are these cupcakes truly safe for a nut-free classroom party?
faq.answer: Yes, if every ingredient label is checked, including sprinkles and food coloring. No nuts or nut-derived ingredients are used in this recipe.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes ahead for a birthday party?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store unfrosted at room temperature in an airtight container. Frost the morning of the party for the best texture.

faq.question: Why is my batter so thin before baking?
faq.answer: Thin batter is normal here because of the hot water. It bakes into a soft, moist chocolate crumb, not a dense cake.

faq.question: Can I swap the buttermilk for something else?
faq.answer: Yes, mix 1/2 cup whole milk with 1/2 tablespoon lemon juice or vinegar and let it sit 5 minutes as a substitute.

conclusion: These chocolate cupcakes prove nut-free baking does not mean flavor-free. Rich, soft, and safe for any classroom or party table.
